$comment: CONSERVATIVE, HIGH-SENSITIVITY BY DESIGN. In an OPD triage context a false
positive costs a nurse a look; a false negative can cost a life. Rules are
therefore written to over-trigger rather than under-trigger, and every
evaluation — fired or not — is persisted so the real rates can be measured
on pilot data instead of asserted.
NO PATIENT-FACING TEXT. The kiosk shows a calm, icon-based, audio-narrated
screen resolved from the localized kiosk bundle; 'staff_rationale' is
clinician-facing only and never rendered to a patient (§14).
critical -> nurse alert + AMPLE fast path + session escalated_to_staff
moderate -> logged and surfaced to the physician; no nurse page
Any change to this file requires the clinical-safety-reviewer agent and must
pass the red-flag regression suite, system-wide, on every PR (§52, §59, §61).

governance.calibration_status: UNCALIBRATED — thresholds and sensitivity are placeholders until pilot data exists (§53)

rules.name: Possible acute coronary syndrome — crushing or pressing central/left chest pain
rules.reference: Chest pain of crushing/pressing character in a central or left-sided distribution is the classic ACS presentation and mandates immediate assessment.
rules.staff_rationale: Chest pain described as crushing or pressing, located centrally or on the left. Pattern consistent with possible acute coronary syndrome. Immediate triage assessment and ECG required.

rules.name: Possible acute coronary syndrome — chest pain radiating to arm or jaw
rules.reference: Radiation to the left arm or jaw is an independent high-specificity ACS feature.
rules.staff_rationale: Chest pain radiating to the arm or jaw. Independent ACS indicator; immediate triage assessment and ECG required.

rules.name: Chest pain with breathlessness, cold sweating or fainting
rules.reference: Autonomic features accompanying chest pain widen the differential to ACS, pulmonary embolism, aortic dissection and pneumothorax — all time-critical.
rules.staff_rationale: Chest pain with autonomic features (breathlessness, cold sweating, or fainting). Differential includes ACS, pulmonary embolism, aortic dissection, pneumothorax. Urgent triage required.

rules.name: Tearing pain — possible aortic dissection
rules.reference: Tearing or ripping pain, particularly radiating to the back, is the characteristic descriptor of aortic dissection.
rules.staff_rationale: Pain described as tearing. Possible aortic dissection — do not delay for routine intake. Immediate senior assessment required.

rules.name: Possible acute stroke — one-sided weakness, speech or vision change
rules.reference: Sudden focal neurological deficit is time-critical; thrombolysis windows are measured in minutes.
rules.staff_rationale: Sudden one-sided weakness, speech difficulty, or vision change reported. Possible acute stroke — activate the stroke pathway and record time of onset immediately.

rules.name: Worst-ever headache or headache with neck stiffness
rules.reference: Thunderclap headache suggests subarachnoid haemorrhage; headache with neck stiffness suggests meningitis.
rules.staff_rationale: Worst-ever headache and/or neck stiffness reported. Differential includes subarachnoid haemorrhage and meningitis. Immediate assessment required.

rules.name: Seizure or loss of consciousness
rules.reference: A first seizure or any loss of consciousness requires assessment before the patient waits in a queue.
rules.staff_rationale: Seizure or loss of consciousness reported. Patient must not be left unattended in the waiting area. Immediate assessment required.

rules.name: Severe respiratory distress
rules.reference: Breathlessness as the presenting complaint with high reported severity indicates respiratory compromise.
rules.staff_rationale: Breathlessness as presenting complaint with severity 8/10 or above. Assess airway, saturation and respiratory rate immediately.

rules.name: Breathlessness lying flat
rules.reference: Orthopnoea is a cardinal feature of decompensated heart failure.
rules.staff_rationale: Breathlessness when lying flat. Suggests decompensated heart failure or significant fluid overload. Prioritise for assessment.

rules.name: Coughing blood
rules.reference: Haemoptysis warrants prompt evaluation for tuberculosis, malignancy and pulmonary embolism — all with public-health or time-critical implications in this setting.
rules.staff_rationale: Haemoptysis reported. Evaluate for tuberculosis (with appropriate infection precautions), malignancy and pulmonary embolism.

rules.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
rules.reference: Haematemesis or melaena indicates active GI bleeding with risk of rapid haemodynamic deterioration.
rules.staff_rationale: Vomiting blood and/or black or bloody stool reported. Active gastrointestinal bleeding — check haemodynamics now and secure IV access.

rules.name: Allergy history with airway swelling or collapse
rules.reference: A documented reaction involving facial/lip swelling, breathing difficulty or collapse indicates prior anaphylaxis and a high re-exposure risk.
rules.staff_rationale: Reported allergic reaction involving airway swelling, breathing difficulty or collapse — prior anaphylaxis. Flag prominently before any drug administration and confirm the culprit agent.

rules.name: Severe pain
rules.reference: Self-reported severity of 8 or more warrants prompt analgesia review irrespective of cause.
rules.staff_rationale: Patient reports severity 8/10 or above. Prompt analgesia review required irrespective of underlying cause.

rules.name: Sudden severe onset
rules.reference: An abrupt, maximal-at-onset presentation is characteristic of vascular catastrophes.
rules.staff_rationale: Symptom described as sudden and severe at onset. Abrupt maximal-at-onset presentations are characteristic of vascular events; do not defer assessment.

rules.name: Reduced urine output or blood in urine
rules.reference: Oliguria suggests acute kidney injury or obstruction; frank haematuria requires prompt evaluation.
rules.staff_rationale: Reduced urine output and/or blood in urine. Evaluate for acute kidney injury, obstruction or urological pathology.

rules.name: Unexplained weight loss
rules.reference: Weight loss with night sweats or persistent fever is a recognised indicator of tuberculosis or malignancy, both prevalent in this population.
rules.staff_rationale: Unexplained weight loss with night sweats and/or persistent fever. Evaluate for tuberculosis and malignancy; consider infection precautions.

rules.name: Patient stopped prescribed medication on their own
rules.reference: Self-discontinuation of chronic therapy is a common and correctable cause of decompensation.
rules.staff_rationale: Patient reports stopping prescribed medication without medical advice. Establish which medicine, for how long, and why, before prescribing.

rules.name: Documented allergy alongside active medication
rules.reference: Co-existing allergy and active polypharmacy is the highest-yield point to check for a contraindicated agent already in use.
rules.staff_rationale: Patient has a documented allergy AND is taking medication. Verify no contraindicated agent is currently in use before prescribing.

rules.name: Symptom brought on by exertion
rules.reference: An exertional trigger is the defining feature of stable angina and of exertional dyspnoea from cardiac cause.
rules.staff_rationale: Symptom triggered by physical exertion. Suggests an ischaemic or cardiac-limitation pattern; assess before the patient is asked to walk or wait standing.

rules.name: Severe debility on AYUSH assessment
rules.reference: Very poor Bala with absent Ahara Shakti indicates a patient too depleted for routine outpatient throughput, irrespective of system of medicine.
rules.staff_rationale: AYUSH intake indicates very weak strength and/or complete loss of appetite. Patient is significantly depleted — assess hydration and nutrition before routine consultation.

rules.name: Cannot exert at all — AYUSH Vyayama Shakti
rules.reference: Breathlessness on mild exertion or complete exertional intolerance is a cardiorespiratory finding regardless of the department the patient walked into.
rules.staff_rationale: AYUSH intake reports breathlessness on mild exertion or complete inability to exert. Cardiorespiratory assessment indicated alongside the AYUSH consultation.
